title: Limiter hot-path resilience and fairness tuning for bursty workloads
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: Multiple recent incidents showed our quota enforcement and global rate limiter can cause prolonged application degradation during short high-volume bursts and when a regional limiter becomes long-tail offline. This ticket defines a pragmatic, low-risk plan to make the limiter hot path resilient, improve fairness across tenants during bursts, and provide safe fallback behavior when limiter nodes are unhealthy.

Goals:
- Meet token-level SLOs: 99.9% request-level success for control-plane operations and 99% for user-facing generation requests under expected burst profiles.
- Reduce tail latency amplification when burst traffic arrives across clients by using smoothing and temporary soft-allowance.
- Ensure multi-region failover minimizes per-customer unfairness and avoids global overload cascades.
- Provide an outage-mode fallback that degrades gracefully (probabilistic sampling + conservative per-customer cap) until limiter is recovered.

Design summary and trade-offs:
1) Burst smoothing: introduce a local in-memory short-bucket (2s sliding window) that allows controlled short bursts above configured steady-state rate using a damped token refill (token-bucket with dynamic refill rate). Trade-off: small temporary oversubscription vs reduced 429 spikes; safe because refill bounded and will be audited in telemetry.
2) Fairness lanes: implement tenant-weighted fairness by exposing two local queues per limiter instance: priority (latency-sensitive customers) and best-effort. A tunable fairness scalar ensures heavy clients cannot monopolize burst allowance. Trade-off: added complexity to hot path and additional queue metrics.
3) Circuit breaker + outage mode: if >30% of limiter cluster signals unhealthy or median RPC latency > 2s for 15s window, switch clients to a fallback policy: local probabilistic allowance (p=0.25 default), strict per-customer emergency cap (configurable, defaults to 100 requests/min per tenant), and emit deprecation metrics. This avoids cascading retries and gives apps ability to detect degraded enforcement.
4) Multi-region failover: prefer region-local enforcement; on region-control-plane loss, route enforcement to nearest healthy region with per-region dampening to avoid simultaneous burst bleed into a single region. Route decision uses topology weight table that is rate-limited and cacheable for 60s.

Acceptance criteria (tests & telemetry):
- Load test: synthetic uniform and Zipfian burst tests show 50% reduction in 429 spike amplitude and 30% reduction in p95 tail latency under same QPS compared to baseline.
- Chaos test: force limiter-node flapping across a region; services should transition to outage mode within 20s and recover without exceeding global error budget.
- E2E: No regression in steady-state throughput and unit cost should not increase >3% under normal traffic.

Implementation plan (high-level tasks):
- Task A: RFC review + config additions (Miguel) — design document and SLO thresholds in Confluence.
- Task B: Local smoothing + token-bucket change (ENG hot path) — implement and microbenchmark.
- Task C: Fairness lanes + per-tenant weights proof-of-concept (ENG).
- Task D: Circuit breaker detection rules + outage-mode policy + client-side hinting header.
- Task E: Multi-region routing policy and topology caching.
- Task F: Observability: new dashboards, per-tenant burst telemetry, canary alerts.
- Task G: Staged rollout: internal canary -> infra canary -> 5% traffic -> 25% -> 100% with automated rollback on SLO alerts.

Rollout constraints and safety knobs:
- Feature gated via runtime flag 'limiter_resilience_v1' and per-customer opt-out.
- Emergency kill switch in Console for instant global rollback.
- Default behavior is off for Dedicated/Private until validated in Hosted.

Links & artifacts:
- RFC: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Limiter+Resilience+RFC
- Load test harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/loadtests/tree/main/limiter-bursts
- Initial implementation PR (smoothing): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1234
- Fairness lanes POC PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1250
- Incident postmortem that motivated this work: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INC/2024-11-06-Limiter-Partial-Outage

Open decisions:
- Thresholds for circuit breaker (30% unhealthy vs 50%): prefer conservative 30% for first rollout, evaluate telemetry after 2 weeks.
- Default probabilistic allowance in outage mode (0.25) subject to change based on customer impact tests.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: local smoothing could allow attackers to burst through budgets. Mitigation: cap absolute burst tokens per tenant and add adaptive backpressure by reducing refill for offending tenant across cluster.
- Risk: fairness lanes add code complexity on the critical path. Mitigation: keep queueing micro-benchmarked and optionally disabled behind runtime flag.

Next steps:
- Schedule RFC review on 2025-01-20 with SRE, runtime, product and support.
- Miguel to open the limiter-resilience feature flag and create migration checklist.
